statusText: EA_ON - Tail 17 of 100 in the low band, below the watch and block thresholds; Stress 73 high; Confidence 86 high.
recommendation: Mapped policy state moves to EA_ON as Tail eases to 17. The closing sequence granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 printed a marginal new session low at 28,899.43, bought it back and settled at 28,937.84, while NQ futures stopped at 29,277.00, roughly 66 points above their own 29,210.50 low, before the CME maintenance pause. The whole session spanned 0.84% and VIX closed at 17.20, well below its 18.03 session high, so volatility never confirmed the price low. This clock hour contains no price discovery at all, which removes the only mechanism by which a Tail path could develop within it. Stress remains high at 73 because the backdrop has not improved: the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.01% after an intraday 5.04%, the highest since 2007, the 2-year is 4.67% for a continued bear-steepening, and WTI is $105.48 with Brent $108.50 following the Saudi East-West pipeline outage. A live FOMC decision with a Summary of Economic Projections is scheduled for 18:00Z on 16 September and the press conference from 18:30Z; that sequence is the published danger window of 18:00Z to 19:30Z and the only part of this horizon mapping to the block band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closes at 28,937.84, down 0.65%, after buying back a marginal new session low, and NQ halts at 29,277.00 well above its own low as the futures maintenance pause removes price discovery, easing Tail to 17 with Stress high at 73 into Wednesday's live FOMC decision
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index settled at 28,937.84, down 189.32 points or 0.65% from a 29,127.16 previous close, having opened at 29,100.16 and traded a session range of 28,899.43 to 29,142.80, a span of about 0.84%. The structural observation that carries this hour is the shape of the close rather than its direction. The index printed a marginal new low at 28,899.43, was bought back from it, and settled roughly 38 points higher. NQ futures agree: their final trade before the CME daily maintenance pause was 29,277.00, down 0.59%, about 66 points above their own 29,210.50 session low and more than 200 points below the 29,495.25 high. A market that sets a marginal new low and then recovers is granting mean reversion, which is precisely the behaviour whose sustained absence defines a Tail path. This clock hour compounds that: between the cash settlement and the futures reopen there is no meaningful price discovery, so there is no mechanism by which persistent one-way structure could form inside it. Volatility supports the same read. VIX finished at 17.20, up 0.58% on the day but well under its 18.03 session high and barely above a 16.79 session low. Volatility declining to a fresh price low, inside a day range under nine tenths of one percent, describes pressure without disorder. Cross-asset conditions remain the source of that pressure and are why Stress stays in the high band at 73. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.01% after reaching 5.04% intraday, the highest since 2007, while the 2-year is 4.67%, the 5-year 4.83% and the 30-year 5.37%, so the curve continues to bear-steepen. WTI trades $105.48, up about 4.0%, with Brent at $108.50, after attacks forced Saudi Arabia to shut its East-West pipeline; reporting puts as much as 4% of global supply at risk and repair estimates range from very soon to eight weeks. Index internals were dispersed rather than uniformly weak: the semiconductor complex finished firm while several megacaps closed materially lower, which is a mixed regime rather than a directional one, and the dominant mode is recorded as mixed for that reason. The scheduled path from here is well defined. U.S. August retail sales are released at 12:30Z on 16 September, the last major data point before the decision, and the FOMC statement with the Summary of Economic Projections follows at 18:00Z with the press conference from 18:30Z. Market pricing has carried roughly a 93% implied probability of a 25 basis point increase, which would be the first in more than three years, so the unpriced content sits in the projections and the guidance rather than in the headline rate. That sequence is structurally multi-stage, with an initial statement reaction, a press conference and a potential delayed second leg through the bond market and then equities, and it is the only part of this horizon where conditional Tail is mapped into the block band. The published danger window is therefore narrow: 18:00Z to 19:30Z on 16 September. Evidence quality is high but marginally below the closing hour because no live price path exists while futures are halted. The cash close and range, the final futures print and range, VIX, the 2-year, 5-year, 10-year and 30-year yields, WTI and Brent, the FOMC pricing and the U.S. calendar were each verified directly against primary sources. The shared cross-asset context file collected at 20:28:55Z was consulted as delayed supporting evidence only; it reports a partial collection with its calendar section unavailable, so it was used solely as confirmation and never as live price-path evidence. On the points that matter it agrees with the verified picture, showing the Nasdaq-100 future down 0.56%, the VIX future up 1.18% and well off the day's high, crude up 4.44%, Treasury futures lower across the curve, five of seven semiconductors higher and only two of eight megacaps higher. That agreement supports Confidence at 86 without altering the Tail or Stress judgement, which rests on the independently verified cash and futures structure.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail ranged from 14 to 25 and entered the block band in exactly one hour, the 08:00Z European-morning slot. The U.S. evening and Asian stretch was the calmest of the cycle, with Tail between 14 and 16 from 21:00Z through 03:00Z as the overnight range compressed. The European morning lifted risk twice, at 05:00Z and 08:00Z, both recorded as trend-down. Through the Tuesday U.S. session Tail rebuilt from 18 at 11:00Z to a 24 peak at 15:00Z as the index worked lower and the 10-year pushed above 5%, then eased steadily to 20 by 18:00Z, ticked to 21 at 19:00Z on the power-hour retest of the session low, and returned to 20 for the closing hour once that low was bought back. Stress held in the high band for the entire U.S. session, between 70 and 77, and Confidence stayed between 86 and 89 throughout. The cycle was one of persistent cross-asset pressure assessed on consistently good evidence, not a single disorderly episode.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail sits at 17 for the current maintenance-pause hour, where no price discovery takes place, then eases to a horizon floor of 14 across the 01:00Z to 02:00Z Asian stretch that matched the calmest hours of the published lookback. From the European pre-market it rebuilds stepwise, re-entering the watch band at 07:00Z and peaking for the European morning at 21 in the 08:00Z slot that carried the prior cycle's only block-band reading, before easing through the late-European lull to 19. It then steps to 22 for the 12:00Z hour containing the retail sales release and 24 for the 13:00Z hour that carries both the data digestion and the U.S. cash open, the highest pre-decision reading on the horizon. After a mid-session ease the final approach lifts it from 22 at 16:00Z to 24 at 17:00Z as liquidity thins, and the horizon tops at 28 in the 18:00Z slot containing the FOMC statement, the Summary of Economic Projections and the start of the press conference, holding at 26 through the 19:00Z question period. Those two slots are the only part of the horizon mapping to the block band and they bracket the published danger window of 18:00Z to 19:30Z. The final cash hour returns to 23 on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly once the projections are absorbed. Confidence decays from 86 to 59 across the horizon as verified live evidence gives way to conditional reasoning.
